track-little-bear-024.title: Emily's visit

lines.text: Today must be a special day.
Enhe, Emily is coming to visit today.

We are having soup and sandwiches and fruit and cake…Oh yes, your favorite bowl.
Hello Emily, why don't you come inside?
Oh this is Lucy, she talks to Emily.
Well, I'm going to work in the garden today.
And this is my good luck twig that I found deep in the forest.
What kind of good luck does it bring?
You'll hold on to the end, and I'll hold on to the other.
And now we run a round and a round in the room.
Look, see, the twig found my seashell.
Father Bear brought it back for me from the ocean.
Yes, maybe he is always in a fishing ship and he is probably catching a fish right now.
These are Mother Bear and Father Bear's all cloth.
Now you really look like Father Bear.
Pleased to meet you, young lady.
Lovely day for a stroll in the garden.

Oh, yes, a perfect day for fishing too.
But Father Bear we'll get my new dress dirty.
Don't worry, I'll get you a new one.
Oh, Father Bear, you are so generous.
You have to be careful with boats.
Oh, find a perfect fishing spot.
This looks like a perfect spot.
Not so good, I think the fish are sleeping.
Lucy thinks you and I are a very nice couple and should get merried.
Enhen, she says two people who fish so well together should get merried.
But how do we do that?
Well, first we need a wedding bouquet.
No, somebody has to say the words.
Can you say the merry words?
Oh, yes, I can do that.
Wait, I'm supposed to hold the flowers, and you hold the ring.
Did you take Emily to be your offerly wedded wife?
Emily, did you take Little Bear to be your lovely wedded husband?
And I was supposed to hold it.
I'm supposed to give you a ring too.
But I only have one elastic band.
Owl should now pronounce you Little Bear and Friend.
Well，that's what wedding banquets are for.
That's my favorite part of being merried.
Of course Owl, you've taken such a fine job.
You looked lovely in that dress, dear.
Thank you, Mother Bear, Come on, slowpokes.

It's my favorite kind of weather.

Father Bear likes quiet when he is reading the paper.
Remember if we listen carefully, we can hear the sound of the ocean.

You just have to know how to do it.

lines.text: I was just thinking that I have to go back to school soon.

So one day it will be a big oak tree.

That's because we are all friends.

Because I offered her a piece.

On no, I found it sitting on the windowsill when I came in.
It looks so good I had to have a piece right away.
And he gave me a piece too.
I wonder would anyone else likes some pie?

track-little-bear-087.title: The Campfire Tale
track-little-bear-087.textSource: /Users/wangtianlong/工作/未命名文件夹/4、little bear 台词本43本/The Campfire Tale.doc

lines.text: That's the biggest moon I have ever seen.
Yes, it's a beautiful sight, little bear.
I wish I could take it back and show it to mother bear.
I know a story about a little bear who wanted to do the very same thing.
En ha, this little bear was away from his mother bear and missed her very much.
Oh, he must be a little little bear.
You see, he missed his mother bear so much that he wanted to take the moon back to her as a present.
But you can't do that, the moon is too far away.
Well, this little bear knew that.
But he thought if he could scoop up the moon's reflection out of the water, he could carry it home to his mother bear in a bucket.
Hello, moon, I'm going to take you home and show you to mother bear.
Back and forth he went, spoonful after spoonful, night after night……
But it's not the real moon in the water.
Oh, this little bear knew that, because his friends had told him.
I know who his friends are.
Yes, I believe you are right.
Little bear, what are you doing?
I'm putting the moon in this bucket.
Why, is it going to fit?
I'm going to give it to mother bear as a present.
He kept spooning one spoonful after another.
I think the moon is shrinking.
I still don't see any moon in the bucket.
Was the moon really getting smaller?
Night after night, the little bear was making progress.
Look, the moon is half gone.
Oh, the bucket is half full.
So the moon was in the bucket.
Well the little bear hoped so.
Because one night the bucket was full and the moon was gone.
Oh, I don't see it, but I know it is in there.
So little bear carried the full bucket back to mother bear.
And did he give it to her as a present?
What did you get there, little bear?
I brought you a present, mother bear.
I spoon some of it out of the lake every night.
Well, then I'm sure it's in there.
Little bear picked up the bucket and put it in the corner of his room.
Hello, moon, I know you are in there.
He waited and waited, but night after night, the moon stayed hidden.
There was no moon in the bucket, and no moon in the sky.
I don't think the story is over yet.
No, not at all, you see that's why the little bear's friends came to see him.
We want to talk to you.
And we were wondering when you were gonna put the moon back.
Maybe the moon doesn't belong in the bucket.
Mother bear, I have to put the moon back into the sky.
It was a dark night, the clouds filled the sky.
As the little bear carried the bucket back to the lake, his mother bear and all his friends were with him.
He waited in the lake, lifted the bucket and through the water into the lake.
There it is, the moon is back.
I am glad the moon is back, where it belongs and where everybody can see it.
Look mother bear, isn't that the biggest moon you have ever seen?
Ah, it certainly is, little bear.
And so the moon was back in the water and back in the sky.
And so he did it, uncle Rusty, he did give the moon to his mother bear.
And now whenever his mother bear looks up the sky and sees the moon, she knows the little bear can see the moon, too.
Thank you for the story, uncle Rusty.

To see if a glass of water at night, just like me?

And do you write him things about me?
I'm sorry you missed the sunrise, little bear.
But I did see the sunrise.
Then you are a lucky little bear.

And Lucy fell down the tree.

But I think you should go home now.
I don't want you catching the mumps.

She is a little sour, too.
I have a present for you.
Come inside, little bear, don't worry, you have already had the mumps, grandma says you would not catch them again.

Is that you and me at the hop frog pond?

Mother bear had drawn the story for me.
But I have told her what's your write.
Emily is little bear's best friend, he hopes she gets better soon.
